items.excerpt: 1. France Imposes Curfews After Nationwide Riots (France) 2. Italy Plans Troop Deployment Amid Widening Protests (Italy) 3. Gaza Food Aid Cuts Leave Half a Million Without Support (Middle East) 9. Japan Launches Mission to Return Samples From Mars Moon (Space) 10. Trump’s Approval Falls to 31% Before US Midterms (US) ... French authorities have imposed overnight curfews in Paris and several other cities following a weekend of nationwide protests that descended into widespread rioting and looting. More than 2,500 people have been arrested, with at least two deaths reported and around 1,000 police officers injured. More than 2,000 businesses were affected, with damage estimated at hundreds of millions of euros. ... Italy’s government plans to deploy 500 troops to Milan after weekend protests over rising living costs and public services descended into rioting and looting. Deputy Prime Minister Matteo Salvini announced the move ... Ukraine’s 92nd Separate Assault Brigade says it has evacuated a wounded soldier from the front line using an aerial drone, in what it describes as a world first. The soldier was lifted by an Ayudag-6 hexacopter and taken to a safer position, where comrades arranged his transfer to hospital. He is now undergoing treatment and rehabilitation. ... Both Ukraine and Russia rely extensively on battlefield drones, creating areas where movement carries substantial danger. Ukraine has previously used unmanned ground vehicles to retrieve casualties but this is its first reported aerial evacuation. Australian independent MP Helen Haines remains in critical but stable condition after a driver allegedly struck her with a vehicle outside her electorate office in Wangaratta, Victoria, on Monday. Ms. Haines has lost one leg already as a result of the attack and doctors are fighting to save the other one. Witnesses said the vehicle turned towards the 65-year-old lawmaker before hitting her. Haines was airlifted to Melbourne. A 43-year-old man remains in custody. Police believe he acted alone. ... US President Donald Trump said he would consider a three-way summit with Russian President Vladimir Putin and Chinese President Xi Jinping, but insisted its focus should be nuclear disarmament rather than Ukraine. Putin reportedly proposed talks alongside next month’s APEC summit in China to discuss ending the war. Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov confirmed discussions about a meeting but said neither its format nor agenda was settled. ... The World Food Programme has cut monthly food assistance in Gaza from 1.6 million people to 1.1 million after its funding fell to less than half previous levels. Families now receive one food parcel instead of two, cash payments have been reduced, and daily hot meals have fallen from 250,000 to 150,000. The agency warns that recent improvements in food security could quickly reverse. ... World Food Programme Palestine director Shaun Hughes said recovery investment was essential because the humanitarian operation was unsustainable. Reconstruction promised after the October 2025 ceasefire has not begun. The agency needs $450 million to maintain critical operations across Gaza and the West Bank through March. Japan launched its Martian Moons Exploration spacecraft aboard an H3 rocket on Tuesday, beginning a five-year mission to collect samples from Phobos, the larger of Mars’ two moons. The spacecraft separated successfully after launch from Tanegashima Island. No mission has previously returned material from Mars or either moon, and earlier attempts to reach Phobos have failed. ... US President Donald Trump’s approval rating has fallen to 31%, the lowest of either presidential term, as rising fuel prices weigh on voters ahead of November’s congressional elections. A Reuters/Ipsos poll found 47% of registered voters favour Democrats against 35% for Republicans, widening the opposition’s lead from seven to 12 percentage points in two weeks. ... The shift follows the US-Israeli war against Iran, which began in February and drove up petrol prices. Some 68% disapprove of Trump’s handling of the economy, including 37% of Republicans. Women favour Democratic congressional candidates by 50% to 32%. ... The November 3 elections will determine control of Congress, where Republican losses could complicate Trump’s remaining agenda. Other surveys reinforce the warning: an NBC poll found 71% believe the country is on the wrong track, while a separate poll put Trump’s approval at 33%. National polling cannot capture every local electoral contest.

items.title: Fed sees AI boom adding to inflation headache, but others may pay for the medicine By Reuters
items.excerpt: CLEVELAND, Oct 19 (Reuters) - The artificial intelligence boom, increasingly acknowledged at the Federal Reserve as helping drive inflation, has left central bankers faced with cooling the rest of the economy to lower price pressures amplified by an industry of marquee names like Amazon, Apple and Anthropic considered immune to rate hikes. Fed officials know their blunt tool of raising borrowing costs lands unevenly. With AI firms spending as if money is no object, economists see the pain of rate hikes falling elsewhere, on firms and families more reliant on credit, or small- and medium-sized businesses that temper their investment plans as borrowing costs escalate. "There are paths to get there," ADP Chief Economist Nela Richardson said of the Fed’s 2% inflation goal, unmet for more than five years. "It’s just not every road is open," with the housing market already weak, for example, and the labor market not seen as a source of inflation through rising wages. ... "What’s left? Small businesses, because they need bank loans, consumers who need to fund payments out of debt and credit cards...Maybe the ... The Fed meets October 27-28 and is expected to keep rates steady at 3.75%-4.00%. Fed officials say further hikes are likely needed and are now debating the pace and extent.

The Dow Jones Industrial Average rose 1%, while drops for several big technology stocks including Apple and Meta Platforms weighed on the Nasdaq composite, which ended down less than 0.1%. items.title: Wall Street gains as healthcare stocks rally, oil prices fall By Reuters
items.excerpt: Oct 20 (Reuters) - The Dow led Wall Street higher on Tuesday as investors focused on value stocks such as healthcare, while technology lagged after rebounding a day earlier. Healthcare led gains among the S&P 500’s 11 major sector indexes and was up 2.3% after hitting a record high. Big gainers included drugmakers, such as Eli Lilly, up almost 4% and the biggest boost to the benchmark index, and Moderna, up more than 5%. ... Real estate and utility sectors were also outperforming, with both up more than 1%, along with the small cap Russell 2000 index, which added 1.7%. Declines in megacap stocks pulled the communication services sector down. Energy shares were flat as oil prices dipped after touching a five-month high. Traders were weighing a meeting between the Iranian president and Pakistan’s army chief, a key US-Iran mediator, against Houthi attacks on Saudi infrastructure and reports of vessel attacks in the Gulf. TECH STOCKS UP SLIGHTLY ... At 2:08 p.m. ET (1808 GMT), the Dow Jones Industrial Average rose 518.51 points, or 1%, to 52,485.50, the S&P 500 gained 31.24 points, or 0.4%, to 7,721.44 and the Nasdaq Composite gained 54.84 points, or 0.2%, to 26,482.94. ... General Motors shares dropped more than 8% and were the S&P 500’s biggest laggards, after the automaker signaled pressure in coming months from higher commodity costs and lower truck sales. 3M gained 5.9% after the company said it was expanding its data-center partnership with Amazon and issued a warrant to an Amazon subsidiary to purchase 3M common stock worth over $521 million. The industrial conglomerate also raised its full-year profit forecast. ... Credit reporting firm Equifax jumped more than 10% after it reported third-quarter profit above analysts’ estimates. It was among the S&P 500’s biggest percentage gainers on the day, along with Hasbro. The toymaker gained 10% after it raised its full-year forecast for both overall revenue and its digital gaming business.

items.excerpt: John Turturro, thief of New York characters, adds a capstone in 'The Last Pickpocket in New York' NEW YORK (AP) — John Turturro grew up in Hollis, Queens, and has lived in Park Slope, Brooklyn, since 1988. Through his life as a New Yorker, his most reliable reservoir of inspiration has been the sidewalks and subway cars around him. Turturro’s latest New York character, an aging pickpocket in “The Only Living Pickpocket in New York,” has brought him something rare for the much-loved but relatively seldom-honored actor: Oscar buzz. His soulful performance could land him his first nomination. 'The Simpsons' resurrects Apu after nearly a decade of silence The Halloween-themed episodes of “The Simpsons” have always been a treat of spooky stand-alone storylines. On Sunday, the show surprised viewers with the resurrection of Apu. The beloved Indian Kwik-E-Mart operator had not been heard onscreen in almost a decade. Once voiced by Hank Azaria, he's now voiced by Indian American actor Sunil Malhotra. Apu’s surprise return is a remarkable twist to a long-running discourse about the character representing a painful stereotype to some South Asian Americans. Comedian Hari Kondabolu made the 2017 documentary “The Problem With Apu.” He commended “The Simpsons” on bringing Apu back. ... Richard Riehle, dependable TV and film character actor who was in 'Glory' and 'Office Space,' dies NEW YORK (AP) — Beloved character actor Richard Riehle has died at 78. Wright Entertainment Inc. announced Monday that Riehle died on Oct. 15. Riehle's career spanned nearly five decades, with memorable roles in “Office Space,” “Glory,” and “The Fugitive.” He often played authority figures but was equally skilled in comedy. He began acting at the University of Notre Dame and later earned a Masters of Fine Arts from the University of Minnesota. Riehle appeared in three “Star Trek” series and on Broadway. He is remembered for his talent, kindness, and support for emerging actors. ... The live-action “Moana,” featuring Dwayne Johnson as Maui,” debuts Wednesday on Disney+. The original animated version is also available. On Friday, “The Invite,” starring Seth Rogen and Olivia Wilde, streams on HBO Max. In gaming, “Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4" launches Friday, this time set on the Korean Peninsula. “Nintendo Switch Sports Resort” arrives Thursday, offering 12 events including bowling and tennis for up to eight players online. New television series include the fourth season of Netflix's “Lupin” and a three-episode “Vanderpump Rules” series set in Las Vegas. Can DC blend horror with a superhero movie? 'Clayface' wants to blur genres NEW YORK (AP) — Superhero films and horror have usually stayed on separate sides of the multiplex. But DC Studios' “Clayface” is the rare attempt to meld the two movie genres. “Clayface” is something unusual in the normally calculated realm of comic book movies. It’s R-rated. It’s also modestly budgeted at $40 million. And it stars the relatively unknown Tom Rhys Harries as a little-known DC villain. And it comes at a pivotal time for James Gunn and Peter Safran's DC Studios, following the box-office flop of “Supergirl” and the Warner Bros. merger with Paramount.

items.excerpt: Entertainment News (10/21/26) - BusinessWorld Online # Entertainment News (10/21/26) PRODUCER, songwriter, and multi-instrumentalist Ziv has teamed up with rising P-pop girl group VVINK for “Trisikulo,” a pop track on the familiar third-wheel experience. October 20, 2026 | 6:06 pm ## Ziv, VVINK release collaboration PRODUCER, songwriter, and multi-instrumentalist Ziv has teamed up with rising P-pop girl group VVINK for “Trisikulo,” a pop track on the familiar third-wheel experience. Released under Sony Music Entertainment, it is built around Filipino wordplay that links a tricycle’s three wheels to the feeling of being the extra person in someone else’s love story. The song was co-written by Ziv alongside Paolo Benjamin Guico of Filipino folk-pop band Ben&Ben and Angelika Samantha Ortiz, one of the songwriters behind BINI’s hit “Pantropiko.” The mixing was also done by Jacques Jenkins and mastering by Luna Tebbs. The track is out now on all digital music streaming platforms. ## *Love in Disguise* premieres on Prime Video *LOVE in Disguise*, a Korean series based on the hit web novel *Why Don’t You Know It’s a Girl?*, has premiered on Prime Video. It is directed by Park Dhan-hee and stars Yim Si Wan, Seorina, Kim Junghyun, and Yeonwoo. The genre-blending romance is exclusively seen on Prime Video in the Philippines and in more than 240 countries and territories worldwide. ## Estelle Fly drops club-pop single SINGAPOREAN pop artist Estelle Fly has released “Shut It Down,” a playful club-pop single about switching off the overthinking and making the dance floor your own. Inspired by the Rihanna and Kesha songs, the new release is an invitation to let loose, dance with friends and have fun even when life feels complicated. It is out now on all digital music streaming platforms. ## Cayabyab, APO, Mitch Valdes reunion THIS holiday season, National Artist for Music Ryan Cayabyab, OPM legends APO, and performer Mitch Valdes will come together for *naRyan nAPO Kami*, the fourth chapter of the MaestroClass Concert Series. The shows will be held on Dec. 4, 5, and 6 at the Proscenium Theater at Rockwell Center, Makati. All shows take place at 7:30 p.m. Joined by the Ryan Cayabyab Singers, the special Christmas chapter of the concert series brings together familiar songs, stories, and artists in a celebration that captures the warmth and spirit of a Filipino family gathering. Tickets are available directly at the Proscenium Theater website via *https://prosceniumtheater.com/* and at the Power Plant Mall Cinema. ## *Amir* gets international distribution GMA Pictures, GMA Public Affairs, and Brightburn Entertainment have officially locked in a partnership deal with Columbia Pictures for the distribution of the upcoming fantasy-drama film and 52 nd Metro Manila Film Festival (MMFF) finalist *Amir*. It is directed by Zig Dulay, with a script crafted by National Artist for Film and Broadcast Arts Ricky Lee alongside Anj Atienza. The film’s cast features Dennis Trillo, Argus Aspiras, Glaiza de Castro, Will Ashley, Caprice Cayetano, Epy Quizon, Joel Saracho, Ronnie Lazaro, Laila Ulao, Heath Jornales, Yasser Marta, Mad Ramos, Ethan Hariot, Hebron Ecal, and Mon Confiado. ## Rachel Chinouriri releases new album UK’s indie-pop singer-songwriter Rachel Chinouriri has released her second studio album, I think I spoke too soon, via Atlas Artists/Parlophone Records. The album expands upon the pop, indie, and rock influences that Ms. Chinouriri has long used to sketch portraits of her inner world. The album’s focus track is “Pretty girls,” which celebrates women, self-confidence, and the freedom to express oneself without fear of judgement. ## M2M 2027 world tour has Manila leg NORWEGIAN pop duo M2M have announced that their global tour *TWO* will be coming to Manila in 2027. The tour will start in March and after concerts at Mexico, Singapore, Hong Kong, and Jakarta, M2M’s global tour will reach Manila on April 2, 2027, at the Araneta Coliseum in Quezon City. Tickets will go on sale on Oct. 24 at 10 a.m. via *TicketNet.com.ph* and TicketNet outlets nationwide. Presented by Wilbros Live, the concert will feature M2M performing their greatest hits, “Don’t Say You Love Me,” “Mirror Mirror,” “Pretty Boy,” and “The Day You Went Away,” among others. ## Maris Racal appears in Maya Black’s music video ACTRESS Maris Racal is featured in Maya Black’s latest music video, serving edgy looks against a hyperpop track. In the video, everything she wants turns into a miniature version of itself, bringing the song’s “make it mini” message to life. The idea behind it is all about having more flexibility when it comes to bigger purchases, to promote Maya’s Mini Payments offering. The music video starring Maris Racal can be viewed here: *https://youtu.be/b\_zKjZ6u2f4?si=q8AzbC9iUSLp0sAV*. With Mini Payments, eligible purchases made using the Maya Black credit card can be converted into three, six, nine, or 12 monthly payments.
